boundary_rationale: The row opens on a direct second-person prohibition, וְאַתָּ֞ה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בְּעַד הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.7.16, byte tier) — ‘ve-attah al-titpallel be'ad ha-am ha-zeh,’ ‘and you, do not pray for this people’ — turning the address from the people back to the prophet himself, a discourse-frame imperative distinct from the temple-gate proclamation before it. The forbidden intercession is grounded in the offerings to the “queen of the sky” described at 7.18, the women knead the dough, to make cakes to the queen of the sky (web:Jer.7.18), and the unit closes on the consequence clause לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה (oshb:Jer.7.20, byte tier) — ‘lachen koh amar Adonai YHWH,’ ‘therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh’ — which keeps the same divine speaker as the prohibition and is retained by its own consequence connective, lachen ('therefore'), rather than by a shared referent: the prohibition's own referent is הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה, 'this people' (oshb:Jer.7.16, byte tier), while the closing verse's is הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה, 'this place' (oshb:Jer.7.20, byte tier) -- a different noun, not a recurrence of the first. The place-noun is itself a catchword reaching back across this row's own front seam to וְלַ֨מָּק֔וֹם (oshb:Jer.7.14, byte tier), 'and to the place,' which argues cohesion with the material just before this unit rather than within it. oshb:Jer.7.20 is also the book's only koh-amar adonai-YHWH stack (sweep: 1 verse), a uniquely attested title site; the mouth does not change here, so the formula marks emphasis rather than a fresh address.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The therefore-clause at 7.20 could open its own row as a fresh koh-amar onset, but it continues the same divine speaker and the same topic as 7.16-19 rather than naming a new addressee or scene, so the consequence is kept inside the prohibition unit rather than split from it.

The whole complex closes at 25:29's declaration that Yahweh is calling for a sword against the earth. boundary_rationale: A prose-sermon superscription opens the unit, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.30.1, byte), matching “The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.30.1) — the hadavar-asher-hayah shape that opens the consolation core's own parent frame. A command to write follows without any change of speaker, כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּתָב לְךָ֗ אֵ֧ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶל סֵֽפֶר (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte), matching “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.” (web:Jer.30.2) — write every word spoken into a book. The content commanded to be written follows at once, closing on the promise itself: כִּ֠י הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְ֠שַׁבְתִּי אֶת שְׁב֨וּת עַמִּ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִֽיהוּדָ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֗ים אֶל הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥תִּי לַאֲבוֹתָ֖ם וִֽירֵשֽׁוּהָ (oshb:Jer.30.3, byte), matching “For, behold, the days come,’ says Yahweh, ‘that I will reverse the captivity of my people Israel and Judah,’ says Yahweh. ‘I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.’” (web:Jer.30.3). A third-person rubric then names what has just been given, וְאֵ֣לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶל יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.30.4, byte), matching “These are the words that Yahweh spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah.” (web:Jer.30.4) — dropping out of quoted divine speech into the narrator's own summary of it. The imperative that follows at verse 2, כְּתָב לְךָ֗ אֵ֧ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶל סֵֽפֶר (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte), is a commissioning write-command addressed to the same figure the header already names, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.30.1, byte), so the address is specified rather than reopened; the messenger formula standing at the same verse involves no frame-owner change: the mouth stays the same across these verses, so neither form reaches the internal-seam classes that cut, and the whole four-verse frame stands as one unit. A fresh koh-amar opens the first poem at verse 5, matching “For Yahweh says: ” (web:Jer.30.5), and this row stops short of that onset.
